I have resolved the issue by encoding the fully qualified domain name with `idna` (punycode) in [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-sjx6akxy/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L17) in [django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-sjx6akxy/django/core/mail/utils.py).

### Summary of Changes
- **[django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-sjx6akxy/django/core/mail/utils.py)**: Updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-sjx6akxy/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L17) to convert `socket.getfqdn()` to an ASCII-compatible encoding (punycode) via `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`. This ensures non-ASCII hostnames are converted to punycode when generating `Message-ID` headers or opening SMTP connections.
